transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My sleep has been all over the place—some nights I’m up planning and working on music, and other nights I can’t sleep at all or I sleep half the day. It's really starting to mess with my life, and my wife was worried enough that she urged me to come in and get some help.

During the times when you stay up planning and working on music, do you also feel unusually energized or euphoric, need much less sleep without feeling tired, or act more impulsively than usual? Or is it mainly that you want to sleep but just can’t?

It's definitely not that I want to sleep and can't—I actually feel incredibly energized and wired during those times. I'll only sleep about three or four hours, but I wake up buzzing with ideas and feel completely fine, like sleep is just getting in the way of my projects. I just have this restless energy where I'm constantly jumping from my laptop to my guitar and back again.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt very down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day? If so, did it happen at a different time from these energized periods?

Yes, I definitely experience those heavy, down periods, and they are completely separate from my energized times. In fact, this current low stretch has been hanging over me for about three months, ever since a big work contract fell through. I've actually been cycling back and forth between these highs and lows since my early twenties.

During your energized periods, have you ever become so impaired that you were hospitalized, had psychotic symptoms like hearing things or having fixed false beliefs, or got into major trouble because of reckless behavior? Or were those periods more noticeable to others but not that severe?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, had hallucinations, or gotten into extreme trouble like that. It’s definitely noticeable to others—especially my wife, who constantly points out my pacing and fast talking—but it's never been severe enough to make me lose touch with reality.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent distinct mood episodes since early adulthood, with hypomanic periods marked by elevated energy, decreased need for sleep, pacing, fast speech, and increased goal-directed activity, alternating with clearly separate depressive episodes lasting at least several weeks. The current episode is depressive and there is no history of psychosis or hospitalization during elevated periods, supporting bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression.
